verses.text: On the first day of the third month, in the eleventh year, the LORD's message came to me:
"Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and all his crowds of people: 'Who can be compared with you in your greatness?
Think of Assyria, once a cedar in Lebanon, with beautiful branches shading the forest. It was very tall, and its top reached above the thick branches.
The waters made it grow, and deep springs made it tall. Their streams flowed all around the place where it was planted, and they sent channels to all the other trees of the field.
So it grew taller than all the trees of the field. Its branches grew many and long because of the plentiful water.
All the birds of the sky nested in its branches. All the wild animals gave birth under its branches. All the great nations lived in its shade.
It was majestic in its beauty, with its long branches, because its roots went down to plenty of water.

The cedars in the garden of God could not compare with it. The pine trees could not equal its branches, and the plane trees could not match its boughs. No tree in the garden of God was as beautiful as it was.
I made it beautiful with its many branches, and all the trees of Eden, the garden of God, were jealous of it.'
So this is what the Lord GOD says: 'Because it grew so tall, lifting its top above the thick branches, and because it was proud of its height,
I handed it over to the ruler of the nations, to deal with as its wickedness deserved. I threw it out.

Foreigners, the most ruthless of nations, cut it down and left it. Its branches fell on the mountains and in all the valleys. Its boughs lay broken in all the ravines of the land. All the nations of the earth came out from its shade and left it.
All the birds of the sky settled on its fallen trunk, and all the wild animals lived among its branches.

So no other trees by the waters will ever again grow proudly tall, lifting their tops above the thick branches. No other well-watered trees will ever reach such a height. For they are all doomed to die, to go down to the world below, among the people who go down to the pit.'

This is what the Lord GOD says: 'On the day it went down to the grave, I made the deep springs mourn for it. I held back its streams, and its plentiful waters stopped flowing. I covered Lebanon with gloom because of it, and all the trees of the field withered away.

I made the nations shake at the sound of its fall when I brought it down to the grave with those who go down to the pit. Then all the trees of Eden, the finest and best of Lebanon, all the well-watered trees, were comforted in the world below.
They too went down with it to the grave, to join those killed by the sword. Those who had lived in its shade among the nations, its allies, went down with it.

Which of the trees of Eden can be compared with you in splendor and greatness? Yet you too will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the world below. You will lie among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his crowds of people, says the Lord GOD.'"
